bib.title: Chapter 4: Assembling the Context Engine (Context Engineering for Multi-Agent Systems)

question: How do you move from a hardcoded chain of agents to an adaptive system that plans and executes multi-step tasks over specialist agents?
contributions: A Context Engine with a Planner, Executor and Tracer, a plan-execute-reflect rhythm
An Agent Registry whose capability descriptions are the Planner's context
Context chaining via $$STEP_N_OUTPUT$$ placeholders resolved by resolve_dependencies()

limits: No evaluation: one example run, no metrics, no baseline against a hardcoded pipeline.
Model, temperature and call_llm_robust internals are not shown here (the text names GPT-5 only as an example LLM).
'MCP' here is a homegrown message envelope (create_mcp_message), though the quiz calls it the Model Context Protocol.
Chapter says it will be hardened for production (context management, guardrails, error handling) in chapter 5.
Reflect is named in 'plan, execute, reflect' but no reflection step is built; only Planner, Executor and Tracer exist.
Hardcoded flow: plan is not re-planned on failure; any step error halts the run.
practices: Separate planning from execution: the Planner emits a JSON plan, the Executor runs it (Architecting the Context Engine).
Describe each agent's role, inputs and outputs clearly in the registry, because the description quality sets plan quality (Agent Registry).
Use a standard message envelope between agents so the Executor passes data without translation (specialist agents).
Resolve $$STEP_N_OUTPUT$$ placeholders on a deep copy of the inputs, so the plan is not mutated (Executor).
Validate the plan, accept a dict wrapping {'plan': [...]}, log the raw LLM output on failure and raise to halt (Planner).
Fall back to a neutral instruction when no blueprint is found so the workflow completes (Librarian).
Tell the synthesis LLM to focus strictly on provided facts to mitigate hallucination (Researcher).
Keep a trace of plan, planned input, resolved input and output; return it even on failure (Tracer); explainability is a requirement in some regions, e.g. the European AI Act (Running the engine).

terms.definition: a meta-system, an intelligent controller that organizes specialized agents around a high-level goal
the output of one agent becomes the input for the next, giving a stateful workflow
a central directory that turns a collection of agents into a coordinated team
a stored instruction (JSON) for how a kind of writing should be structured or styled, retrieved by intent
the Tracer: logs the goal, plan, each step's agent, planned input, resolved context and output, status and duration
